figures.caption: Table 1: Summary of the experimental procedures, temporal data structure, and analysis strategy for the three experimental paradigms.

Figure 1: Conceptual schematic of the experimental and data-analysis pipeline: An electrophysiological recording of total duration T is divided into a pre-intervention baseline period of duration Tb and a post-intervention period. The latter is further divided into N temporal windows of duration Tj , each of which is compared with the baseline window using a measurable discriminator of network activity. Changes in the discriminator between the baseline and post-intervention windows are quantified using the metric ∆ (Eq. (2) in this work). The discriminator may be based on the mean firing rate (MFR) or on statistics derived from the interspike interval (ISI).

Figure 2: Determination of the significance threshold for changes in a given discriminator from vehicle-control recordings. Empirical distribution of the contrast index (∆) derived from vehicle-only experiments. The dashed lines indicate the 5th and 95th percentiles of the empirical control distribution, used as the lower and upper response thresholds, respectively. In this example the analysis is shown for mean ISI, µISI.
Figure 3: Classification of electrode-wise responses based on the normalized change ∆ξ relative to the natural fluctuations observed in the control or vehicle condition.

Figure 4: Description of the compositional analysis: Each post-intervention window j is further segmented into shorter temporal segments. In each segment, all active electrodes are classified into one of three response states, as described above and in Figure 3: excited (E), inhibited (I), or unchanged (U). The resulting distribution of electrode states defines the compositional state vector, illustrated in the figure as a gauge representing its relative composition.

Figure 5: Temporal activity classification and representation within the excitation–inhibition–unchanged (EIU) space. (a) Example of experimental data from a single MEA electrode, showing the normalized mean inter-spike interval (ISI) over time. The upper and lower thresholds, derived from control recordings, define the boundaries used to classify temporal changes in electrode activity. (b) Three-dimensional EIU space representing the relative contributions of excited, inhibited, and unchanged activity. Each electrode is mapped within this space according to its computed excitation, inhibition, and unchanged state (sE , sI , sU ), such that its position reflects the relative contribution of each activity state over time.
Table 2: Network discriminators considered in the analysis and their interpretation in terms of neuronal network activity.

Figure 6: Time-dependent response profiles across experimental paradigms. Comparative overview of the temporal response patterns observed across the different experimental paradigms. The reorganized representation highlights the evolution of the measured responses over time and facilitates direct comparison among experimental conditions, emphasizing both shared temporal trends and paradigm-specific differences.Data are presented as group means ± SEM, where n represents the number of independent MEA cultures analyzed per experimental group.

Figure 7: Static EIU composition and group-level metrics across experimental conditions. The left column shows the distribution of each experimental group within the excited–inhibited–unchanged (EIU) activity-state simplex, where position reflects the relative contributions of faster-spiking (E), slower-spiking (I), and unchanged (U) activity states across the complete observation period. The middle and right columns show the corresponding response-direction balance (η) and responsiveness (R), respectively. Points represent group means and error bars indicate the standard error of the mean (SEM). The sample size (n) indicated for each condition represents the number of independent MEA cultures included in the analysis. Rows correspond to the 4-AP intervention, optogenetic stimulation, and external benchmark datasets. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.

Figure 8: Time-resolved EIU composition and group-level metrics. Temporal evolution of network activity within the excited–inhibited–unchanged (EIU) activity-state framework across experimental conditions. The EIU simplex plots show the trajectories of each group over successive time points, illustrating changes in the relative contributions of faster-spiking (E), slower-spiking (I), and unchanged (U) activity states. The corresponding time-resolved metrics, η and R, quantify response-direction balance and overall network responsiveness, respectively. The upper panel presents the 4-AP/drug-condition groups (AP100, AP10, Water, and Medium), whereas the lower panel presents the light-stimulation groups (ArchT-LS, Spontaneous, and LS). Together, these representations illustrate both the direction of activity-state transitions within the EIU space and the temporal evolution of the associated network-level metrics from 5 to 30 min. Points represent group means and error bars indicate the standard error of the mean (SEM), with n representing the number of independent MEA cultures analyzed per experimental group. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.

Figure 9: Comparison of effect-size magnitude between ∆ and R statistical approaches across Peak, DKL, µ, and MFR metrics. Individual points represent absolute Cohen’s d values, while larger markers indicate the mean and error bars show 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Dashed reference lines denote small (d = 0.2), medium (d = 0.5), and large (d = 0.8) effect-size thresholds.

Figure 10: Neuronal activity 24 h after 4-AP removal and characterization of the neuronal culture. Cultures were exposed to 4-AP for 30 min, after which the drug was removed and the cultures were washed. Mean firing rate (MFR) was reassessed 24 h later to evaluate whether neuronal activity persisted following 4-AP removal. Water-treated cultures served as controls. Individual paired measurements are connected by lines, showing the change in MFR between the initial (Before) and 24-h follow-up (After) recordings. Each connected pair represents one independent MEA culture measured before and 24 h after treatment. Statistical comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; exact p-values are indicated above each group. The persistence of neuronal activity 24 h after 4-AP removal is consistent with the reduced activity observed following 4-AP exposure reflecting a prolonged adaptive or desensitizing response rather than a complete loss of neuronal activity.
